questions.explanation: A memorial garden's spatial argument includes path, enclosure, and focal point. Plants alone are insufficient.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: The narrative a war memorial selects
questions.learningObjective: Predict memorial narrative
questions.stem: A sports club bulletin on a war memorial asks what narrative it likely selects; what is expected?

answer.exemplar: A war memorial likely selects a narrative of sacrifice and collective memory, honouring the dead while shaping how the community remembers the conflict.

questions.explanation: War memorials typically select sacrifice and collective memory. They shape community remembrance.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: The limit a cast sets on reproduction
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate cast reproduction limits
questions.stem: A sports club bulletin counts 4 casts from one mould; if detail degrades each generation, how many are first-generation?
questions.explanation: Only the first cast is first-generation, so 1. Later casts lose detail.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: What a photographic negative documents
questions.learningObjective: Synthesise negative documentation

stimulus.body: A sports club bulletin explains that a negative records light as dark and dark as light. It is the intermediate step before a positive print.

questions.stem: What does the negative document in the bulletin?

options.text: A tonal inversion of the scene

questions.explanation: The negative documents a tonal inversion of the scene. It is an intermediate, not the final image.

questions.subject: ART_HISTORY
questions.topic: The direction of an intaglio image
questions.learningObjective: Apply intaglio direction knowledge
questions.stem: A sports club bulletin prints an intaglio plate; which way will the image face?
questions.explanation: The printed image is reversed, a mirror image of the plate. It is not identical or merely colour-inverted.
